title: Mahadji Shinde
subtitle: The Maratha master of Delhi · c. 1730 – 1794
subject: mahadji
intro: The youngest son of Ranoji Shinde survived Panipat crippled, rebuilt his family's fortunes, defeated the British at Wadgaon, brokered the Treaty of Salbai, and became regent of the Mughal empire — with a European-trained army that made him the strongest power in north India. He died at the height of his power, while trying to consolidate it at the Peshwa's court in Pune.

context.label: Mahadji – head of the Shinde house

events.title: Born to Ranoji Shinde
events.summary: Mahadji is born, the youngest son of Ranoji Shinde, one of Bajirao I's leading commanders.

events.title: Campaigns with his brothers
events.summary: He learns war in north India alongside his brothers Jayappa and Dattaji.

events.title: Dattaji killed
events.summary: His brother Dattaji is killed fighting the Afghans at Burari Ghat.

events.title: Wounded at Panipat
events.summary: At the Third Battle of Panipat Mahadji is badly wounded and escapes, lamed for life — rescued, by tradition, by a water-carrier who later served him as a trusted officer. His nephew Jankoji is captured and executed.

events.title: Head of the Shinde house
events.summary: After years of disputed succession, Mahadji is recognised as head of the Shinde family and its lands in Malwa.

events.title: Back in Delhi
events.summary: With Tukoji Holkar and Visaji Krishna, Mahadji retakes Delhi and escorts the exiled emperor Shah Alam II back to his capital.

events.title: With Nana against Raghunathrao
events.summary: After Narayanrao's murder Mahadji supports the regency council for the infant Peshwa — in an uneasy partnership with Nana Phadnavis that lasts the rest of his life.

events.title: Battle of Wadgaon
events.summary: Mahadji's forces surround a British army marching on Pune with Raghunathrao and force it to sign the Convention of Wadgaon.

events.title: Gwalior fort lost
events.summary: A Company force storms Gwalior fort by night; in 1781 another British column inflicts a defeat on Mahadji in central India, and both sides look for peace.

events.title: Treaty of Salbai
events.summary: Mahadji negotiates peace between the Peshwa's government and the Company. The British recognise him as an independent power, and Gwalior is returned.

events.title: A European-trained army
events.summary: Mahadji hires the Savoyard officer Benoît de Boigne to raise infantry brigades and artillery on European lines — soon the most effective army of any Indian state.

events.title: Regent of the Mughal empire
events.summary: Shah Alam II names the Peshwa his Vakil-ul-Mutlaq with Mahadji as his deputy — in practice making Mahadji master of Delhi, Agra and the emperor's household.

events.title: Setback at Lalsot
events.summary: Fighting the Rajputs of Jaipur and Jodhpur at Lalsot, Mahadji is deserted by many Mughal troops and forced to retreat; he loses control of Delhi for a time.

events.title: Delhi retaken; Ghulam Qadir punished
events.summary: The Rohilla chief Ghulam Qadir seizes Delhi and blinds Shah Alam II. Mahadji's army retakes the city, captures Ghulam Qadir and executes him, and restores the blind emperor.

events.title: Patan and Merta
events.summary: De Boigne's brigades crush the Rajput armies and Ismail Beg at Patan (June) and Merta (September), leaving Mahadji supreme in north India.

events.title: Return to Pune
events.summary: Mahadji comes south to Pune with great ceremony, presenting the young Peshwa with imperial honours — and seeking a larger role at court, which Nana Phadnavis resists.

events.title: Holkar defeated at Lakheri
events.summary: De Boigne's brigades defeat Tukoji Holkar's army — Maratha fighting Maratha in the north.

events.title: Dies at Wanavdi
events.summary: Mahadji dies at his camp at Wanavdi near Pune, aged about 64. His memorial, the Shinde Chhatri, stands there. His young grand-nephew Daulatrao inherits his army.
